what_it_does: When chip designers create digital logic circuits, they often use a technique called Boolean decomposition — breaking complex logical functions into smaller, simpler pieces that standard building blocks can implement. This produces high-quality circuits but is very slow because the search for good decompositions involves checking huge numbers of candidate combinations. EDGE speeds this up by borrowing ideas from database software (the kind that powers web applications and corporate data systems): it re-frames the decomposition search as a database query, letting a mature query optimizer rapidly generate and filter candidate solutions instead of checking them one by one. The paper targets synthesis of Gate-Inverter Graphs (GIGs), a compact way of representing logic circuits used in modern chip design flows.
